answer: Collision-Keyed Memory Ledger: each identity must solve a random seed drawn from a shared fable table, and its solution is stored as an onyx-coded entry. A clone reusing prior work produces a colliding key that the ledger detects instantly. Every new identity also requires a fresh tundra-stamped nonce, so duplicating an agent forces distinct seed solutions per copy. Attacker cost: one unique computation and storage slot per identity, making mass duplication linearly expensive and exposing reuse on first check.
